purpose: Preview art-direction concept board; not finished slides or execution evidence.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Create ONE polished art-direction contact sheet for a Korean technical lecture series called p-hermes. This is a conceptual design board, not a screenshot of an existing implementation and not a finished deck.
Composition: a carefully aligned 2-column by 3-row contact sheet of SIX DISTINCT 16:9 slide studies, separated by narrow neutral gutters. Flat straight-on slides, no perspective mockups, no devices. Use a large high-resolution canvas. Each miniature should have very little text, an excellent oversized Korean title and one dominant visual. The six slide studies must look like a coherent editorial system yet vary in composition.
Visual identity: midnight navy #121D34, warm ivory #F6F4ED, vivid cobalt #315BE7, restrained amber for a difference. Beautiful Korean sans-serif typography, highly considered asymmetric whitespace, sharp alignment, refined native technical drawing aesthetics. Mix dark dramatic openings with bright readable explanations. This must feel engaging, contemporary and professionally art-directed. No gradients, glow, glass, generic card dashboard, robot mascot, decorative 3D blobs, lorem ipsum, stock business people, or huge tables.

Panel 1 top left, dark navy: exact Korean title "에이전트의 구조" with a small p-hermes wordmark. The title is the visual anchor at upper left. At lower right, a spare crisp conceptual map with ONLY five legible labels: "작업", "지식", "카탈로그", "이미지", "영상". Visually group the first three as common supporting responsibilities and the last two as production applications; do not show five obligatory sequential steps. Use generous space and a few thin orthogonal connectors.
Panel 2 top right, warm ivory: exact title "리비전". A bold typographic comparison visual: large "7" on two left-hand requests labeled "A" and "B", large cobalt "8" as the updated shared state, and a restrained amber mark showing the stale B request does not match. Use one precise aligned diagram, not boxed cards. This should feel like the pause just before an outcome is revealed.
Panel 3 middle left, warm ivory: exact title "퇴역". A rich editorial document comparison using clearly recognizable paper records and a search result lineup. An older record remains in the archive while it is visibly absent from the current result lineup. Keep the paper shapes structural and elegant; no shredding or deletion imagery. Use only two short secondary labels "기록" and "검색".
Panel 4 middle right, dark navy: exact title "버전과 내용". Two large identical "v2.0" labels with small aligned schematic metadata rows underneath; one precisely highlighted amber difference reveals that the contents differ. Include elegant cobalt/ivory typographic rhythm. No fake SHA strings, no invented metrics, no long code.
Panel 5 bottom left, warm ivory: exact title "구도". Beautiful photorealistic studio photograph of a minimal teal table lamp, matte curved metal shade, warm light, off-white tabletop, left-positioned subject leaving generous clean copy space to the right. Place the Korean title in that usable space. One subtle cobalt editorial guide shows the allocation of image and copy space. High-end product photography but no product marketing slogans.
Panel 6 bottom right, dark navy: exact title "연속성". A cinematic close-up of the SAME teal lamp split into two adjacent boundary frames with a visible but subtle change in lamp position, making the boundary difference inspectable. Beneath is a narrow three-shot timeline with precise labels "0", "4", "8", "12 s". A single amber vertical playhead aligns to a shot boundary. No decorative waveforms or fake video player buttons.

Render all Korean text cleanly and exactly. Every panel must have a distinct, strong composition rather than the same heading-plus-card layout. This is a visual concept board; accuracy of the described relationships matters, but do not add explanatory paragraphs. No outer headline or watermark.

Edit this p-hermes lecture art-direction contact sheet. Preserve the six design concepts, Korean titles, navy/ivory/cobalt palette, lamp photography, flat editorial style and six-panel order. Make the following precise corrections:
1. The board must have TWO columns and THREE rows of actual 16:9 slide rectangles. The current panels are too wide and short. Use a nearly square canvas with an overall width-to-height ratio of approximately 32:27 (for example 1920x1620 before gutters). Give every panel more height and compose its existing visual with spacious vertical breathing room. Do not crop or stretch existing text or photos.
2. In panel "버전과 내용", remove all invented KB sizes and dates. Keep the two "v2.0" labels and exactly one meaningful schematic metadata difference: left "runtime: alpha", right "runtime: beta", with beta highlighted amber. This is conceptual sample data, not real source evidence. Remove any other detailed rows.
3. In the "퇴역" panel, simplify the paper text to short labels "문서 A", "문서 B", "문서 C". Show A still in records but absent from search. No invented dates.
Preserve large readable Korean headings exactly: "에이전트의 구조", "리비전", "퇴역", "버전과 내용", "구도", "연속성". Keep all six panels. Use no outer caption or watermark. Each panel must feel like a spacious real 16:9 slide, with its own intentional layout and no rounded UI-card shells.

observed: Six intended Korean topic titles are visible.
Dark navy, ivory and cobalt visual direction is coherent.
Final concept simplifies catalog data and shows retired document A outside current results.
limitations: Contact-sheet panels are not finished 16:9 slide layouts.
Generated graph connections and all sample values are conceptual; final slides require native verified data and staged states.
No motion, video playback, presentation-font or learner validation has been performed.
